correctness.rationale: Independently using the reset-age representation, the stationary angle is an independent reset angle plus circular Brownian motion of independent Exp(λ) age. Its nth Fourier coefficient is the nth reset coefficient times λ/(λ+n²Drot), which gives c₁=aμ and c₂=bη. Coupling at the next reset also shows uniqueness of this stationary law. Conditional on the initial angle, the no-reset contribution to the centered velocity harmonic at lag s decays at k=Drot+λ, while on a reset all dependence on the initial angle is lost. Thus the centered lag covariance is exp(−ks)Σ. In planar coordinates 2Σ=(1−|c₁|²)I+H(c₂−c₁²). Integrating over both times and adding independent translational noise yields the displayed G_k(T) and effective tensor under Cov/(2T). For a circle variable Z of mean μ, |E(Z−μ)²|≤E|Z−μ|²=1−|μ|². Any boundary value is realized by the unique mean-preserving law on the endpoints of the appropriate line through μ; a mixture of opposite boundary phases realizes any interior value, and |μ|=1 forces a single atom. This proves the whole affine tensor disk. Isotropy is its containment of zero in the traceless coordinate, so q_*=b/(b+|b−a²|). At positive extremal drift rotate μ to the positive real axis. Equality forces a perpendicular chord for b−a²>0 and a parallel chord for b−a²<0, giving exactly the stated symmetric and antipodal weights. Since b−a²=t(1−2t)/[(4+t)(1+t)²], the transition has q_*=1 and unique deterministic reset; substitution gives v/3 and D+8v²/(27Drot). The four-atom example gives μ=1/2 and η=5/16, hence v aμ=1/4 and K=D+15/64 in each direction. G_k(T)>0 ensures that isotropy is exactly the same criterion at each positive finite time.
residual_risks: Only convex feasibility at admissible prescribed drift is claimed: |μ|>1 is impossible. Rigidity is for the extremal isotropic solution at nonzero drift or the nondegenerate disk boundary, not interior isotropic solutions in general. Translation noise is independent and isotropic, angular initialization is stationary, and equal covariance eigenvalues do not imply rotational invariance of the displacement law.

Conversely one may reflect a law with zero longitudinal-minus-transverse difference across the drift axis and average, preserving the real first moment and removing the off-diagonal entry. Thus the later interval theorem already implies the long-time isotropic speed bound, and its endpoint rigidity implies the extremal laws (with the unit-mean case deterministic). originality.rationale: The supported distinction is the exact full fixed-drift tensor synthesis with arbitrary complex traceless phase, constructive finite-support laws, and its joint interpretation with the all-time covariance. The angular moment balance and circle moment disk are prior mathematical machinery, and the deterministic isotropic point at λ/Drot=1/2 follows from previous fixed-direction diffusivities. A later catalogue item overlaps the arbitrary-law long-time tensor and its sharp longitudinal-minus-transverse projection, with genuine implications for isotropic feasibility and extremizers; these parts are not credited as distinct against that comparator. Its stated interval is not the full off-diagonal disk. The inspected earlier literature does not give the fixed-drift tensor synthesis.
residual_risks: A stronger unlocated orientation-control result might already combine arbitrary iid absolute resets with full tensor attainability. The classical moment disk is not new, and the exact partial catalogue overlap does not settle independent derivation or global priority.

checked_sources: Frozen RESULT.md Finding and scope; deterministic prior transport and catalogue real-projection comparison.
value.rationale: The physical design question is to prescribe mean directed transport while controlling covariance in two dimensions, not to maximize one diffusion number in isolation. Complete feasible-tensor geometry and explicit finite-support realizations allow joint control of diagonal and off-diagonal fluctuations. Stationarity makes the same design apply at every observation time. The extremal isotropic transition is a meaningful comparison of reset protocols, while the complete disk is the substantive addition beyond longitudinal anisotropy alone.
residual_risks: This is an idealized single-particle control theorem with independent absolute Poisson redraws; it does not imply full spatial-law isotropy, or guarantees for initial angular transients or interacting swimmers.
